The Most Exclusive Club in Aviation

There is a club you cannot buy your way into, cannot be invited to, and cannot apply for. The only way to become a member is to have your life saved by a Martin-Baker ejection seat. If that happens, the British company sends you a certificate, a patch, a pin, and a distinctive tie. It’s called the Ejection Tie Club, it was founded in 1957, and it has more than 6,000 members around the world.

Every one of them was, at some point, a pilot in an aircraft that was about to kill them.

That’s the job the ejection seat does, and it does it with staggering violence. In the span of a couple of seconds, a rocket-powered charge blasts the pilot and seat clear of the cockpit, punches them up and away from the doomed aircraft, and deploys a parachute, all while the body endures crushing G-forces that can briefly compress a pilot’s spine. It is brutal. It is also, very often, the difference between a funeral and a reunion.

The engineering has only gotten better. Since 1961, Martin-Baker’s seats have had what’s called “zero-zero” capability, meaning they can save a pilot even at zero altitude and zero speed, sitting still on the runway or tumbling just above the ground, situations that were once a death sentence.

The results speak for themselves. Martin-Baker says its seats have saved 7,827 lives since the first live test in 1945, and the number ticks up a little every year. The company now supplies ejection seats to 93 air forces across the globe.

7,827 pilots who should have died in a burning aircraft instead walked away, went home to their families, and got a tie in the mail.
